title: driver-sql (SQLite, MySQL): after a datetime-to-date publish, an equality filter on a day misses rows written while the field was datetime
body:
domain:server#6 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4cz8zK9vJDPeeVKJ4XP

Filing gate: ① out-of-scope finding of the #32851 os-dev report (6842768512), class a, measured while writing the PR #33000 test. ⛔ Not a claim; triage sets the grade and lane.

## What happens

On SQLite and MySQL, after a field is published `datetime` to `date`, a row written while the field was a `datetime` (an instant with a time of day, e.g. `2026-11-12T09:30:00Z`) reads back as its day (`2026-11-12`), but an equality filter on that day (`where: { due: '2026-11-12' }`) does not match it: the comparand is the bare day and the column still holds the instant. Pre-existing and independent of time zones. Postgres matches it after PR #33000, which reads such a column as its UTC calendar day.

Reach: driver `find()` with an equality filter on the day, after `syncSchema` + `applyPublishedColumnChanges`; measured on the SQLite cell of `sql-driver-32851-date-on-instant-column.test.ts` (the assertion is scoped to Postgres for that reason).

## Expected

A `date` field's filter matches every row whose read presents that day, on every dialect.

## Business reason

After turning a datetime field into a date field, a list filtered to "due on 12 Nov" silently leaves out records created before the change, although they show 12 Nov.

Reader: `domain:server`, `packages/drivers/driver-sql` (SQLite and MySQL filter column expression for a `date` field on a former `datetime` column).
Dedupe: `is:issue is:open datetime date publish equality filter`: only #32851.
